pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK; test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
src/index.js uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id; 'AC-2' tests / and ?view=open after marking item 2 done.
'AC-3' marks 3 and 1 done and expects '✓ First item', '✓ Third item' in id order.
'AC-4' expects all three items in id order with only the done one marked.
'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /; the current view is <strong>, not a link.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Open, closed, empty and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet., and No items yet. in all three views on an empty table.
traffic/routes.json lists both views; 'AC-8' asserts them. tests/traffic-config.test.sh and the traffic.test.js fake app were updated to handle queries.

lenses.note: The change follows the spec's two decisions: the list opens on open items, and the view is a query parameter. The one extra is the traffic-config query-string support, which AC-8 requires and the PR discloses.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each has a named test. All 6 state-table rows have a test. The spec has no later edits.

I could not run the tests here: vitest is not installed (npm test failed with 'vitest not found'). By reading, the assertions check behaviour and would fail if the code were wrong. The existing test/index.test.js still holds, because its items stay open. CI covers the run.
The README describes the new views. The migration follows the append-only rule in CLAUDE.md.

Queries are parameter-free and built from a fixed VIEWS map, which is checked with Object.hasOwn. Titles are HTML-escaped. The empty-table check is an extra COUNT query that runs only when a view is empty.
The view value is allow-listed, so there is no injection path. Nothing in the repository tries to instruct the reviewer.
The change adds a small UI: a nav, ✓ marks and empty-state messages. It is minimal HTML with no styling, and the tests cover its content.
No browser is available. The rendered HTML is covered by response-body assertions in test/done.test.js.
The title and body match the diff. The loosened route regex and the changed fake app are both disclosed, and the statement that no tests were loosened is accurate.
